issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency for the Course instructor property: the problem statement and template declare a Course property/initializer parameter named 'instructor' (String), while the solution's Course class declares the property and initializer parameter as 'lecturer' (String). Additionally, the solution's Developer.attend(course:) implementation references course.instructor, which does not exist in the solution Course class. This mismatch prevents the solution from compiling and confuses students about the correct property name to use when accessing a course's instructor.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Course property name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: rename the solution's Course property and initializer parameter from 'lecturer' to 'instructor' and update all references accordingly (e.g., in Developer.swift change course.instructor to the same property). Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to use 'lecturer' and change all references in code and description to match. Ensure the template, problem statement, and solution use the identical identifier so code compiles and students are not confused.

issues.description: Course instructor property naming mismatch: the problem statement asks for a Course property named "instructor"; the template Course class declares and expects a property named "instructor" (template: Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift, declaration at line 9). The solution Course class instead declares the property as "lecturer" (solution: Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift, declaration at line 10). Additionally, the solution's Developer.attend(course:) implementation references course.instructor (solution: Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift, line 49), which does not match the solution Course property name. This inconsistent naming ("instructor" vs "lecturer") prevents a clear mapping from the problem requirements to the implementation, may cause compile/runtime confusion, and increases cognitive load for students trying to follow or modify the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Course instructor identifier consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: rename the Course property and initializer parameter in the solution from "lecturer" to "instructor" (update all internal references in solution_repository/Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift). Then ensure solution_repository/Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift references the same property name (course.instructor). Alternatively, change the problem statement and template to use "lecturer" everywhere — but pick one identifier and apply it uniformly so students can directly map the requirement to the implementation.
